title: Segment contract
description: The segment contract, as defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #80: the microsegmentation chapter's YAML — the segments of the estate and the rules between them, one contract rendered to N fabrics. Each rule names its id (what a render or a promotion cites), its from and to segments, its direction, type, and port inside the modeled subset, and its mode (audit or enforce); exceptions are TTL-bound with a reason in words and a real expiry date. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/segment); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — segments declared and unique, rule ids unique, the modeled subset enforced (tcp or udp, ingress or egress), ports from 1 to 65535, and exceptions expired against the injected clock.

version.description: Version of the contract. The rule table is versioned like code — a rule table nobody re-reads is a rule table nobody still believes.

reviewedOn.description: Date the contract was last reviewed, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags reviews older than 365 days and dates in the future.

owner.description: The team that owns the contract. A rule table with an owner and a review cadence is the discipline.

segments.description: The segments of the estate. A rule may only join declared segments; the validator flags rules that leave from or enter an undeclared segment.

rules.description: The rules between the segments — the one document every fabric renders. Ids must be unique across the contract: two rules with one id is a render that cannot know which row it renders.

id.description: Rule id, e.g. R1. The renders cite it and the promotion PR names it; findings cite it verbatim.

type.description: The protocol, inside the modeled subset — the gate is honest about what it models, not pretending to full eBPF or CIL semantics.

port.description: The port the traffic enters. A rule that names no real port renders to no real fabric.

direction.description: Which way the traffic flows. The contract must say, not shrug.

mode.description: Audit: observed, not enforced — a candidate awaiting a promotion PR with flow evidence. Enforce: rendered and enforced on every fabric.

exceptions.description: TTL-bound exceptions: temporary allowances with their reason in words and the date they expire. An exception without its expiry is not an exception, it is the rule; an expired one is flagged by the validator.

reason.description: The exception's reason in words — an exception nobody can audit is a hole in the contract.

expiresOn.description: The date the exception expires, YYYY-MM-DD. The validator flags exceptions whose window has passed: an expired exception rendered is a promise the clock already broke.
